current_executor.note: CPython 3.14 tier-2. The executor in flight on THIS thread's dispatch; set/cleared by the eval loop around its own tier-2 execution. Not touched by stackweave. Must not be snapped: restoring one would resurrect an executor into a dispatch that never entered it. CAVEAT -- this build is free-threaded with the JIT OFF (_Py_JIT unset), so the field is always NULL here and the SNAP-vs-OWNER_ONLY question is UNTESTED for a JIT-enabled free-threaded build; revisit if tier-2 is turned on -- see docs/installation.md, 'Interpreter build: the tier-2 JIT is off, TLBC is on'.

holds_gil.note: CPython 3.14. Whether THIS OS THREAD currently holds the GIL; owned end-to-end by CPython's attach/detach (take_gil/drop_gil). A property of the thread's attachment, never of a fiber -- snapshotting it would let a resumed fiber restore a stale bit and desynchronise CPython's own GIL bookkeeping from reality. Not touched by stackweave, and must not be.

remote_debugger_support.note: CPython 3.14, PEP 768. Per-thread control block an external debugger writes into and the eval breaker polls. Thread-level, not fiber-level: privatizing it per fiber would strand a pending debugger call in a parked snapshot (never run) or replay it on resume (run twice). Not touched by stackweave. Note that under M:N a debugger targeting a thread reaches whichever fiber is running there -- a known limitation of multiplexing, not something a snapshot can fix.
